I have not completed the game on any level, however I have gotten past the Imloreth fight on "Blood and Broken Bones". The first challenging fight I had was Imloreth, so I decided to restart on "Death March" even though I had found it too challenging prior.

Based on advice from a user here I have been doing a "no frills" build.

So here is the basic strategy for building - you want to end up where you can use adrenaline both to boost DPS but also allows you to synergize between different disciplines. For example if you go for Bear School heavy armor, you get bonuses for heavy attacking and magic. Pair that with the correct decoction and you get another synergistic bonus by using a combination of quick/heavy attacks and magic.

I am building to take the Undying perk after I have increased my toxicity. It is nice to have enough toxicity ceiling to be able to handle 2 decoctions and still use at least 1 or 2 buff potions. At the very minimum you should be able to use 1 decoction and 3 potions simultaneously.

The largest concept that I haven't understood previously wrt The Witcher 3 is that it isn't optimal to build 1 min/max build or even try to only level up skills that will fit in your assignation menu. For some contracts/missions you might have a different skill that you want to swap out beforehand. This becomes more obvious after you can't possibly activate everything you've leveled up.

So what I am going for is for the top two sets of 3 activation slots to be red on one, blue on the other. Then I will have at least 2 alchemy on the 3rd set and the 4th set will be rotating specialty and more 'frilly' stuff. For example I really enjoy the Yrden glyph traps but they don't do very much at all except in very niche circumstances - so it doesn't make sense to equip it over even basic brown/general buffs.

Finally - Just explore everywhere at first. With the horse, you can outrun anything on Velen. So you should have gone and done every single thing on White Orchard, except for a sunken treasure with level 10 swimming drowners. You need to level up higher and get a better crossbow/bolts.

I have played many different builds and progressed through/past Velen several times - but I never even noticed the military camp in the Southeast.
